reports.name: AAFC Outlook for Principal Field Crops (Canada)

outlook: Grains opened Thanksgiving week mostly firmer. January soybeans were up about 6 cents near $12.27 early Monday after Friday's 13-cent gain, helped by meal demand and a private sale of 100,000 tonnes of soybean meal to Spain, and December corn edged up about 1.5 cents to $4.36 as traders looked for a seasonal low with funds holding a net short of about 71,000 contracts. Minneapolis December spring wheat was nearly unchanged at $6.39 while Chicago wheat slipped about 3.5 cents to $5.71 against a firmer US dollar, and Russia said its 2026 grain harvest has reached 141 million tonnes. ICE January canola was up C$2.50 at C$779.30; cash bids below are from Friday's final Minneapolis report.
